requirement_text.REQ-066: Port src/api/errors.zig (272 lines) and src/api/response.zig (69) as Letflow.Api.Error and Letflow.Api.Response -- the single response/error contract every S4 route emits. Nothing in this batch renders a response body by hand once these exist. errors.zig is an RFC 9457 Problem Details builder. Port: the ProblemDetails shape (type as an absolute URI under a configured base, title, status, detail, plus the trace id field errors.zig carries with a "" default), the per-status constructors (problemNotFound and its siblings for 400/401/403/404/409/422/429/500 -- enumerate them from the Zig source rather than guessing which exist), and serialisation to a JSON body. Emit Content-Type: application/problem+json on error responses, per RFC 9457, and state in the moduledoc whether R-Co does the same or emits application/json (check response.zig's CONTENT_TYPE_JSON usage) -- if Letflow diverges, that divergence is deliberate and documented, not accidental. response.zig defines the canonical HandlerResult (status_code, body, content_type defaulting to JSON) and the typed success constructors that keep positive responses on correct status codes (200 vs 201 vs 202 vs 204). In Elixir the conn IS the result carrier, so port these as functions that take and return a conn (send_json/3, created/2, no_content/1, and the error counterparts) rather than transliterating a HandlerResult struct -- Zig returns a value because it has no conn. State that translation in the moduledoc. SECURITY (INV-4, INV-5): an error body must never carry secret material, a raw Ecto/Postgrex error, or a stack trace -- detail is a caller-safe string chosen by the handler, and an unexpected internal error maps to a generic 500 problem document whose detail does not vary with the underlying exception. Separately, the not-found problem document is the exact response a cross-tenant probe receives (REQ-072 enforces the routing; this requirement guarantees the two bodies are byte-identical by construction, because both go through one constructor).

A new case 20b reportedly asserts the fully-seeded-conn body is byte-identical to the bare-conn body for both exception types, which would trip on reflection of ANY conn field rather than just the listed substrings. result.summary: Step 3b RE-GATE PASSES. The single FAIL from commit 1b7fc8c (AC3's vacuous leak half) is corrected; all six re-derived items confirmed independently from the test source at commits 17afbaa/c64ea26, not from TEST-DESIGNER's report. Scope held narrow as instructed -- nothing already signed off was re-litigated. ITEM 1, THE CORE QUESTION -- ALL TEN RETAINED FORBIDDEN SUBSTRINGS ARE NOW GENUINELY REACHABLE-IN-PRINCIPLE. I did not reason about this on paper: I reconstructed leaky_conn/2's exact pipeline in a standalone script (Plug.Test conn + the two put_req_header calls + the four assigns, driven from a real `rescue e ->` with __STACKTRACE__, for both exception types) and probed the resulting conn for every substring. Results, per substring and per the conn field that carries it: 'hunter2' -> x-db-dsn header value 'postgres://app:hunter2@db.internal:5432/letflow' AND query_string 'debug=hunter2&sql=SELECT+tenant_id' (measured query_string = exactly that, so Plug.Test did parse the query off the path -- this was worth checking, since a path-only conn would have re-created the defect); 'db.internal' -> same header; 'SELECT' and 'tenant_id' -> query_string (and 'tenant_id' additionally via the ArgumentError message assign); 'Elixir.' -> :error_type assign, measured as literally 'Elixir.RuntimeError' / 'Elixir.ArgumentError'; 'stacktrace' -> the x-debug-flags header value 'stacktrace,verbose' plus the :stacktrace assign key itself, so an implementation that inspected conn.assigns or dumped a debug header would produce it; @runtime_message -> :exception_message assign, measured `assigns.exception_message == @runtime_message` TRUE; @argument_message -> same, measured TRUE; 'RuntimeError'/'ArgumentError' -> :error_type and the :error assign holding the struct. Each of the ten is therefore produced by at least one conn field that a plausible leaking internal_error/1 (one that echoed assigns, a request header, the path, or the query string into `detail`) would reach. NONE remains that cannot be produced, so there is no residue of the original defect at smaller scale. I also confirm the split into @shared_forbidden plus per-case message/module-name is correct rather than cosmetic: the ArgumentError's message is NOT refuted against the RuntimeError body, which is right -- that would have been exactly the decorative refute the first version was failed for. ITEM 2, :trace_id NON-SEEDING -- REASONING CONFIRMED CORRECT against lib/letflow/api/response.ex:111-117 and :179-180. send_problem/2 computes `effective_trace_id(problem.trace_id, conn)` and, for the empty trace_id every constructor produces, returns `conn.assigns[:trace_id] || ""`, writing it into the serialised body. Seeding :trace_id would therefore make the refute fail against the CORRECT implementation -- it is a designed reflection channel, not a leak channel, and excluding it is right. It leaves nothing unchecked: the channel at issue is conn.assigns as a whole, and that channel is still exercised by four other assign keys (:error, :exception_message, :error_type, :stacktrace); and case 20b's byte-identity holds regardless, because the bare conn and the leaky conn both lack :trace_id and so both serialise trace_id as "". ITEM 3, leak_surface/1 IS LOAD-BEARING, MEASURED NOT ARGUED. I Jason-encoded a problem document whose `detail` is @argument_message verbatim and measured the two searches: `String.contains?(raw_body, @argument_message)` = FALSE (the raw body carries `column \"tenant_id\" does not exist`, backslash-escaped by Jason), while `String.contains?(leak_surface_output, @argument_message)` = TRUE. So a raw-body-only search would have silently missed a real leak of that exact message, and the decoded-values half of the surface is what catches it. Not decorative. (Note 'tenant_id' alone does match the raw body -- it is the full quoted message that does not, which is precisely the case the helper exists for.) ITEM 4, CASE 20b EXISTS AND DOES WHAT IS CLAIMED -- response_test.exs:317-320, `test "a fully seeded conn yields the same bytes as a bare conn"`, asserts `leaky_body_after_runtime_error() == internal_error_body_after_runtime_error()` and the same for ArgumentError. Both sides are raw resp_body strings, so this is byte-identity, and it is asserted for BOTH exception types as claimed. I agree with the assessment that this is the strongest of the new assertions: it trips on reflection of ANY conn field, not only the enumerated substrings, because the two conns differ in request path, query string, two request headers and four assigns. Combined with cases 17/18 pinning the bare bodies to @internal_body, the chain leaky -> bare -> fixed literal is closed. ITEM 5, AC3'S PRIMARY HALF UNTOUCHED -- confirmed by `git diff 1b7fc8c..HEAD -- test/letflow/api/response_test.exs`: cases 17/18/19 (response_test.exs:283, 289, 296) and the internal_error_body_after_runtime_error/0 and internal_error_body_after_argument_error/0 helpers appear only as unchanged context lines. The single replaced test is old case 20; everything else in the diff is pure addition (leaky_conn/2, the two leaky_body helpers, leak_surface/1, @shared_forbidden, leak_cases/0, case 20b). ITEM 6, MANDATORY MECHANICAL NAME-LENGTH MEASUREMENT -- re-run by me with my own extractor over every describe/test pair in BOTH files (Elixir 1.20.3), not accepted on report. MEASURED: 35 tests total (14 in error_test.exs, 21 in response_test.exs), 0 orphan tests outside a describe block. MEASURED MAXIMUM COMBINED describe+test LENGTH = 81 CHARACTERS: 'internal_error and INV-4 a fully seeded conn yields the same bytes as a bare conn' (response_test.exs:317) -- the case added in rework 1, as TEST-DESIGNER reported. Next longest measured 75 (error_test.exs:164), 73 (response_test.exs:304), 71 (error_test.exs:174), 71 (response_test.exs:296). 81 < 200 (this handoff's ceiling) and 81 << 255 (ExUnit's hard SystemLimitError limit), so the docs/anti-patterns.md hazard is cleared with ample headroom. SPEC AC3/AC7 SECTIONS -- test/specs/REQ-066.md's case 20 is rewritten to state the reachability requirement explicitly, enumerate each forbidden substring against the conn field that supplies it, record the measured raw-vs-decoded result, and document the deliberate :trace_id omission; case 20b is added; AC7 is updated to 35 tests / 81 chars, which matches my own measurement exactly (a spec claiming a number I could not reproduce would have been a FAIL). Grepped both test files and the spec: no TODO, no @tag, no @moduletag anywhere, so nothing new to reconcile on the skip/TODO checks. NO REMAINING GAP. Full suite deliberately NOT run -- TEST-RUNNER owns Step 4; main's pre-existing repo-wide format/warning failures (ISS-0106 / GH#354 / queue task 170) not re-litigated. One non-blocking observation for Step 4, not a gate condition: I verified the seeded values reach the conn by reconstructing the pipeline standalone, but I did not compile test/letflow/api/response_test.exs itself, since compiling it means running it. TEST-RUNNER's Step 4 execution is the first point at which the new helpers are compiled.
